bugs: app/Pricing/PriceCart.php:84 — intdiv by $eligibleTotal with no zero guard. A fixed code on a cart whose eligible lines total 0 cents (for example a free item) throws DivisionByZeroError and returns a 500. Probe confirmed it.

app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:45 — the input is uppercased before lookup, but stored codes are never normalised (no mutator). A code stored as 'summer10' can never be redeemed: the request returns 'does not exist' even when the user types the code exactly. Probe confirmed it.

app/Models/DiscountCode.php:53 — an empty cart with an unrestricted code fails the contains() check. It returns the garbled 422 'This discount code only applies to items in the  category.' (empty category name) instead of a meaningful reason.
antipatterns: app/Pricing/PriceCart.php:23,54-55,78 — converts the Collection to arrays with ->all() and then uses array_map, array_filter and array_fill_keys instead of Collection filter, mapWithKeys and sum
app/Pricing/PriceCart.php:57-65 — two sequential if blocks on the enum where a match expression would read better, and the `$this->spreadFixed(...) + $discounts` array-union trick is opaque
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:45 — manual trim() duplicates the global TrimStrings middleware
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:27-29 — calls discountCode() twice in the ternary (memoised by once(), but noisy)
tests/Feature/ApplyDiscountTest.php:20 — Http::preventStrayRequests() is ceremony; the feature makes no HTTP calls
Validation logic (rejectionReason with user-facing message strings) lives on the Eloquent model, which mixes presentation into the domain
strengths: Thin invokable controller, a FormRequest with an after() hook, and once() memoisation of the code lookup
Laravel 13 #[Fillable] attributes, casts() method and backed enum cast
Explicit integer casts on the money columns
Rejects category-restricted codes when no cart line matches, with a clear message
Factory states (percentage, fixed, freeShipping, expired, exhausted) keep the tests readable
Fixed-amount allocation sums exactly and is capped at the eligible total
Tests cover each 422 reason, boundary thresholds and non-consumption of uses

bugs: A category-restricted code applied to a cart with no matching lines is accepted with 200 and a 0 discount, not a clear 422. This is a debatable design choice rather than a hard spec violation (probe: 'PAT' on a yarn-only cart returned 200 with discount 0).
antipatterns: app/Models/DiscountCode.php:17-23 and app/Models/CartItem.php — no integer casts on value, min_subtotal, max_uses, times_used, unit_price_cents or quantity, so int arithmetic relies on the driver returning native ints
routes/api.php:7 — throttle:30,1 middleware was not requested (minor scope creep)
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:54 — uses load('items') where the controller later calls loadMissing. This is harmless but inconsistent.
strengths: Pricing is built idiomatically with Collections: filter, sum, mapWithKeys and a match on the enum, including an explicit FreeShipping arm
allocate() guards the zero-amount case, so there is no division by zero on zero-value or empty eligible sets (probe confirmed a 200)
The FormRequest keeps all failure reasons in a single match in failureMessage(), so the model stays free of message strings
Uses validated('code') and memoises with once(); the controller is a one-line invokable controller
The pricing action accepts a nullable code, so it can be reused for a no-code breakdown

The most thorough tests: rounding, proportional split values, leftover cents, the exact threshold, empty cart, null expiry or max uses, min_subtotal against the whole cart, and repeated apply not consuming a use
Separate migrations per aggregate, with the enum value used as the column default

v.rationale: I ran the test suites and six edge-case probes on each implementation. Both suites pass (impl-1: 20 tests, impl-2: 24), and I deleted the probe files afterwards. The two implementations are structurally very similar: an invokable controller, a FormRequest with an after() hook and once(), a backed enum, #[Fillable] attributes and an invokable pricing class. The probes separated them. impl-1 returns a 500 when a fixed code applies to eligible lines totalling 0 cents, because PriceCart.php:84 divides by zero. It also uppercases the input without normalising stored codes, so a code stored in lowercase can never be redeemed. On an empty cart it returns a garbled 'applies to items in the  category' 422. impl-2 handled all of these cases gracefully. Its only questionable behaviour is accepting a category code that matches no lines, returning a 0 discount instead of a 422. impl-2 also uses Collections more idiomatically (mapWithKeys, sum, and a match on the enum, where impl-1 uses array_map, array_filter and an array-union trick), keeps the failure messages out of the model, and has broader edge-case tests. impl-1's advantages are explicit int casts and the extra category-mismatch rejection. Those don't outweigh a reachable 500 and an unredeemable-code bug, so impl-2 ranks first.
